week.worked: The armband was right. You put it on B.Fernandes and he scored a hat-trick, and Mbeumo got the fifth in the same game. Before Friday's deadline you sold Mbeumo and Tzolis for Elanga and Cherki, both of them on the house list.
week.didnt: You scored 106 and stayed fifth of 11. Kerkez had one point in two before Friday's clean sheet at Ipswich, and Tzolis was hooked at half-time at Villa Park, so you sold him. You also left the vice-captaincy on Elanga instead of B.Fernandes.

big.call: Captain: Haaland at Old Trafford or B.Fernandes at home to City
big.why: Both are yours. Haaland goes to United, the hardest fixture on his run at 4, three days after a Champions League trip to Porto. B.Fernandes has a hat-trick behind him and City at home. João Pedro at home to Hull is the third option.

You left the vice on Elanga at the GW3 deadline. If Haaland is pulled at Old Trafford, the doubled score goes to a £6.1m Newcastle midfielder at Leeds instead of B.Fernandes at home to City. Moving it costs nothing.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Your club's best player, and you still do not own him. 20 points in two, the penalties, and Hull at home next, then Brentford away.

watchlist.name: Isak
watchlist.note: Two goals in nine minutes at Ipswich and three in three games. You own Calvert-Lewin at £6.0m in that slot. Fulham at home is Isak's next one.

week.worked: You played the Bench Boost in an ordinary week and all 15 of your players started. 151 points, and you lead the five by 29.
week.didnt: Nothing went wrong, so take the cost instead. The chip is spent and the other four hold theirs. Then on Friday you captained Haaland with the rest of the room and benched Calvert-Lewin again, with Leeds at Brighton.

big.call: Captain: with the room or against it
big.why: You lead by 29 with no chip left. The other four will split between Haaland at Old Trafford and B.Fernandes at home to City. Match the majority and the lead holds. Pick the other one and it moves, in either direction.

big.call: van Ewijk and Thomas: Brighton at home, 18 games without a clean sheet
big.why: Coventry have the kindest run on the ticker at 2.33 and both your Coventry defenders sit on the bench. Lampard's side has not kept a clean sheet in 18 matches. That is £8.0m in two defenders you never start.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: 14 points at £5.1m, Burn out until mid-September, and Newcastle have the kindest run after Coventry. You own nobody there, and Elanga is already in two of the other squads.

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: 28 points at £7.1m after two assists on Friday, with Barcola coming off the bench behind him. Schade to Gakpo is £1.1m and you have £0.8m.

week.worked: Gvardiol has 14 points, and City are expected to play him in a back four with Guéhi against a Coventry side that has not scored. On Friday you sold Ndiaye, bought Elanga and Ajayi, and moved Calvert-Lewin into your eleven. All three were on Thursday's list.
week.didnt: 12 points on your bench, second week running, and Calvert-Lewin scored the Leeds equaliser while sitting on it. You fixed that on Friday and then benched Calafiori, who has 20 points and Chelsea at home, behind Hume, who is not in the predicted Sunderland XI.

big.call: Hume or Calafiori: one of them is on the wrong side of your bench
big.why: Sunderland host Arsenal in GW4, so it is the same match. Calafiori has 20 points and you benched him for Hume, who was left out of Sports Mole's predicted Sunderland XI this weekend. Saturday's team sheet tells you which one starts.

big.call: Captain: Haaland at Old Trafford or B.Fernandes at home to City
big.why: Haaland goes to United three days after a Champions League trip to Porto. B.Fernandes has a hat-trick behind him and City at home. You have both, and João Pedro at home to Hull is the quiet third option.

watchlist.name: Konsa
watchlist.note: £0.1m cheaper than Hume, expected to start for Arsenal on Sunday with Mosquera flagged, and Arsenal go to Sunderland in GW4. If Hume is dropped this is the swap.

watchlist.name: Isak
watchlist.note: Three goals in three, two of them inside nine minutes on Friday. You have no bank, so this is a note for when Calvert-Lewin next blanks.

week.worked: De Cuyper has 17 points at £4.7m and you kept him through the Wildcard. Then you played the Wildcard itself from last place, 12 changes, and Gakpo and Jacquet gave you 16 points on Friday night, the most in the room before Saturday's games.
week.didnt: 61 points and last of 11. You were the one gaffer without B.Fernandes on the day he scored three, Tzolis was taken off at half-time, and Aït-Nouri had not played a minute. All three are gone now, and so is your Wildcard.

big.call: Goalkeeper: Raya at Sunderland or Tzolakis at Stamford Bridge
big.why: You have £10.6m in goalkeepers and one of them sits every week. Hull go to Chelsea, who have scored 12 in two games. Arsenal go to Sunderland having conceded none in three. In GW4 the £6.0m one is the starter.

big.call: Captain: Haaland at Old Trafford or B.Fernandes at home to City
big.why: You own both now. Haaland goes to United three days after Porto away in the Champions League. B.Fernandes has a hat-trick behind him and City at home. You are last of 11 and cannot afford the wrong one twice.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: You have no bank and one free transfer next week. If De Cuyper keeps playing as a winger, £5.1m for a left-back who defends in front of the kindest run after Coventry is the move.

week.worked: 107 points without spending a chip, the same week Mr CR7 had. It took a Bench Boost to beat it. You sold Ndiaye on Friday.
week.didnt: 16 points on your bench, the most in the room. Groß scored at Stamford Bridge while sitting on it, and you now start him. You sold Konsa and Ndiaye for Egan and Tzolis, and Konsa is in every predicted Arsenal XI for Sunday while Rogers, at £7.5m, sits on your bench.

big.call: Rogers or Tzolis: your £7.5m midfielder is on the bench
big.why: Chelsea host Hull in GW4, the kindest fixture on Rogers's run at 2. Arsenal go to Sunderland at 3. Tzolis was taken off at half-time at Villa Park and Eze came on for him. You start the £6.5m and bench the £7.5m.

big.call: Captain: Haaland at Old Trafford or B.Fernandes at home to City
big.why: Haaland goes to United three days after a Champions League trip to Porto. B.Fernandes has a hat-trick behind him and City at home. Both are yours, and João Pedro at home to Hull is the third option.

watchlist.name: White
watchlist.note: 18 points at £5.5m in the only defence yet to concede a league goal, expected at right-back again on Sunday. The Special One bought him on Friday. You own the club and none of the players scoring for it.

watchlist.name: Konsa
watchlist.note: You sold him on Friday at £4.4m. Every predicted Arsenal XI for Sunday has him starting with Mosquera flagged. Do not buy him back this week. Watch whether he keeps the shirt when Mosquera is fit.

watchlist.name: Palmer

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: Two assists on Friday, 28 points at £7.1m, and Barcola came off the bench behind him. One of the five owns him.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Four of the five own an Arsenal defender and none owns the £6.6m midfielder outscoring them. Chelsea at the Emirates on Sunday.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: The cheapest attacking defender at a settled club, and Burn is out until mid-September. Newcastle have faced more shots than anyone, so buy him for the attacking returns.

watchlist.name: Konsa
watchlist.note: £55m of centre-back at £4.4m, expected to make his full debut on Sunday with Mosquera flagged and Saliba out for months. One of the five sold him on Friday.

watchlist.name: Araujo
watchlist.note: Debuted at right-back on Friday, kept a clean sheet and took bonus. Liverpool were said to have no right-back. At £5.4m and 2.1% he is the cheap way into a defence with Fulham at home next.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: A hat-trick at Old Trafford, penalties, and all five own him. Everton away, then City at home.
verdicts.trigger: Two quiet weeks with United losing. At £12.0m the price only works while he is the whole team.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Got the fifth against Ipswich and held his flank. Nobody in the room owns him now after two sold him on Friday.
verdicts.trigger: Rashford keeping the left and the returns concentrating there. Two blanks and £8.0m is the wrong United winger.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: Substituted on 73 minutes against Ipswich with muscle tightness and named for a late hamstring test at Everton. Sports Mole expects him to start, with Dorgu the cover.
verdicts.trigger: He starts at Everton and this goes back to solid. He misses it, or Dorgu starts a league game at left-back, and £4.5m is a rotation slot.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: Scored off a deflection and was the steady one in a defence that could have folded. De Ligt is likely to miss Everton, so his place is safer still.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-backs are fit. The goal is a bonus.

verdicts.name: Mainoo
verdicts.why: Started ahead of Andrey Santos against Ipswich, won possession 10 times, more than anyone in the gameweek, and Carrick called him immense. Baleba is out for a couple more weeks.
verdicts.trigger: Baleba fit and starting. £5.5m for a United midfielder who plays every week is a buy. £5.5m for one who plays until the £70m man is fit is a trap.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: 20 points in two games, the penalties, and Chelsea sold Enzo Fernández without signing a replacement. One goal from 50 for the club.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf flag returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Owned by all five, and Sports Mole notes he could be the second player ever to score and assist in each of his first three games of a season. Arsenal away is the hardest fixture on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box. At 71% he becomes the risk in every squad at once.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Three starts from three since the £117m move, and Arsenal wanted him at £80m before Chelsea paid more. One of his three owners has him on the bench this week.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide right or on the bench. The Camara deal collapsing makes that less likely.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: Chelsea have gone 18 games without a clean sheet, have conceded five in two, and go to the Emirates with two stand-ins in midfield.
verdicts.trigger: One clean sheet. Until it comes he is a goalkeeper bought for save points at a club that concedes.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: Came on against Brighton and lasted under 20 minutes before going off again. Alonso called the change precautionary. Sports Mole lists him as a major doubt for Sunday.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. Chelsea never replaced him and the shirt is waiting.

verdicts.name: James
verdicts.why: Alonso says he will get a lot of minutes as a first midfielder and could become one of the best in the world there. He is listed as a defender at £5.5m in a side that has not kept a clean sheet in 18 games.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet, or a goal. A defender in midfield gets defender points for a goal, so the case needs Chelsea to stop conceding.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: 20 points at £5.7m, the assist for Saka's winner at Villa Park, and a clean sheet with it. Four of the five own him and one has him on the bench this week.
verdicts.trigger: The knee trouble that follows him around, or Arsenal's European calendar producing real rotation.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: The only goal at Villa Park, penalties at £9.5m, and Arsenal have sold all three of the wide forwards who were competing with him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or Arsenal buying a forward in January and the returns moving centrally.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Predicted to lead the line against Chelsea with Martinelli, Trossard and Jesus all sold. He and Gyökeres are the entire senior forward line.
verdicts.trigger: Gyökeres taking the shirt outright. Two games on the bench and £7.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Gyökeres
verdicts.why: Zero points in two at £7.3m, but he scored 21 in his first season and Arsenal are down to two senior forwards.
verdicts.trigger: A start and a goal in the next two. A £7.3m striker who has not scored by GW5 is not a striker.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: 14 points at £6.6m and a fortnight of nobody in the room owning him.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or the returns concentrating in Saka alone.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: 18 points at £5.5m in the only defence yet to concede a league goal. Timber is back in full training but Sports Mole has him on the bench at best on Sunday.
verdicts.trigger: Timber starting a league game at right-back. He is one week closer than he was on Thursday.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: The flag arrived on Saturday morning, 75%, two days after he missed Thursday's open training. Every predicted Arsenal XI for Sunday has Konsa in his place. Nobody in the room owns him now.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea puts this back to solid. A second missed game and Konsa has the shirt through the international break.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: Expected to make his full Arsenal debut against Chelsea with Mosquera flagged and Saliba out for months. £4.4m, and one of the five sold him on Friday.
verdicts.trigger: Chelsea's visit. He starts and keeps a clean sheet and this goes to solid. Mosquera plays and £4.4m stays a bench place.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Predicted to start against Chelsea on the left after Arsenal sold both other left-sided forwards. Le Professeur bought him on Friday.
verdicts.trigger: A second half-time substitution, or Eze starting ahead of him. Then it is a sack and it stays one.

verdicts.name: Eze
verdicts.why: He set up Saka's winner after coming on at half time. Sports Mole has him on the bench again against Chelsea behind Tzolis.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea. If Arteta gives him the shirt in that fixture the price is wrong by a long way.

verdicts.name: Bruno G.
verdicts.why: Flagged at 75% with a knock after missing Thursday's training. Sports Mole expects Lewis-Skelly and Rice in the pivot on Sunday.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea. Until then £6.8m buys a player nobody has seen finish a week fit.

verdicts.name: Raya
verdicts.why: Three clean sheets from three at £6.0m. The Special One bought him on Friday and put him on the bench behind Tzolakis.
verdicts.trigger: Two goals conceded in a game. Until then the question is which of his owner's two goalkeepers plays.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: All five captained him for Coventry at home, a side that has not scored this season. City's only striker after Marmoush left.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury. City spent a record fee and did not buy a back-up, so there is no version of this where he plays less.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Predicted to start at left-back in a back four with Guéhi against Coventry. Two of the five own him now.
verdicts.trigger: Doku back and City going wider with O'Reilly restored to defence. Nothing said this week points that way.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Sports Mole's predicted XI has him back at centre-back beside Dias, with Anderson and Bouaddi in the pivot and O'Reilly out of the side. Coventry have not scored.
verdicts.trigger: Two league starts in midfield. A defender who never stands in the back four cannot keep a clean sheet, whatever the shirt says.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Still the highest-scoring midfielder in the game, and three of the five bought him this week. Predicted at ten again behind Haaland.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts in a row at number ten. He has never reached ten Premier League goals in a season, and Enzo Fernández is now in the building.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: One assist all season at £8.5m. Sports Mole expects him to keep the flank ahead of Ndiaye against Coventry.
verdicts.trigger: A goal against Coventry at home. If it does not come in that fixture, £8.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: City signed him for depth, behind Cherki and Foden at ten and Semenyo and Foden wide. Both of his owners in the room sold him on Friday.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. Nobody here owns him and nobody should.

verdicts.name: Barcola
verdicts.why: Came on for Muñoz on 64 minutes at Ipswich. Iraola said he had not played a minute since the World Cup and had to be careful.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts on the left. At £8.0m he needs the shirt, and the first team sheet has not given it to him yet.

verdicts.name: Isak
verdicts.why: Two goals inside nine minutes at Ipswich, three in three, and Iraola took him off on 64 with the game won. 23 points at £9.0m and nobody in the room owns him.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without a shot on target. Fulham at home is the next read, then Bournemouth away.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: Friday's trigger was Barcola starting on the left. Barcola started on the bench and Gakpo made both goals, then moved to centre-forward when Isak came off. 28 points at £7.1m.
verdicts.trigger: Barcola's first start on the left with Gakpo on the bench. Iraola says he values him, and Friday looked like it.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Thursday's trigger was a game at right-back. Araujo debuted there instead and Szoboszlai drove Liverpool's midfield. Three of the five own him.
verdicts.trigger: One game at right-back. A full-back does not take spot kicks, and the penalties are the case at £7.0m.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Thursday's trigger was a clean sheet at Ipswich or against Fulham, and it came on Friday. He started, was troubled once by Fatawu's pace, and was never in real difficulty.
verdicts.trigger: Two goals conceded at home to Fulham. Then the clean sheet was Ipswich's finishing and £5.5m is back to watch.

verdicts.name: Jacquet
verdicts.why: Clean sheet beside Van Dijk at Ipswich, 9 points at £5.0m, and the BBC called him a very fine acquisition. One of the five bought him on the wildcard.
verdicts.trigger: Dropped for Konaté or two goals conceded at Anfield. A £5.0m centre-back who starts every week is the price to own.

verdicts.name: Araujo
verdicts.why: Made his debut at right-back at Ipswich and was rated seven for it. The club that failed to sign a right-back had one in the squad.
verdicts.trigger: Frimpong back in the shirt. Two starts and a £5.4m right-back at a club that keeps the ball becomes a buy.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: Everton's only senior striker after Beto left and the Balogun deal collapsed, at £5.5m, with United at home.
verdicts.trigger: Everton signing a free agent forward, or two blanks against United and Spurs.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Grealish is back on loan from City and Sports Mole says an immediate return to the XI is not out of the question. The creative share is no longer his alone.
verdicts.trigger: Grealish starting and taking the set pieces. Then £6.5m is the second creator at a club with one striker.

verdicts.name: Tarkowski
verdicts.why: Everton's captain on set pieces, 18 points, and United visiting a ground that will spend the afternoon shouting at its own directors' box.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without a header or a clean sheet. Then this is a set-piece bet.

verdicts.name: Elanga
verdicts.why: Opened the scoring at Spurs, 17 points at £6.1m, and Jaissle says Fernandez-Pardo will be eased in from the bench. Two of the five bought him this week.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo starting on his flank. That is the only thing that ends this.

verdicts.name: Wissa
verdicts.why: Scored at Spurs, Woltemade has gone to Juventus on loan, and Osula is out. The shirt is his at £6.1m.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo being played centrally, or two blanks in the easiest run in the league.

verdicts.name: Hall
verdicts.why: 14 points at £5.1m in the side with the softest run after Coventry. No team has faced more shots than Newcastle this season, so the returns are at the other end.
verdicts.trigger: Burn returning around 14 September and the left side going back. Until then this is the cheapest attacking defender at a settled club.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: Three of the five start him against Leeds. Brighton are missing six, including Wieffer at right-back, and Leeds are improvising at centre-back without Rodon.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against Leeds. A £4.5m goalkeeper is bought for this fixture, and both defences are makeshift.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: 17 points at £4.7m, and Sports Mole's predicted XI has him in the attacking three again with Kadioglu at left-back.
verdicts.trigger: A return to left-back and a clean sheet. £4.7m for a makeshift winger is the wrong position at the wrong price.

verdicts.name: Groß
verdicts.why: Crossed for one and headed in another at Stamford Bridge, on penalties at £5.5m. Both owners in the room now start him.
verdicts.trigger: Two weeks without a return. At 33 the minutes are the question.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Scored again, started again, and Nmecha came on to play beside him rather than replace him. All five own him and one benches him.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or Leeds changing the shape around him.

verdicts.name: Wilson
verdicts.why: Four points in two at £6.4m, and Leeds go to Brighton with Calvert-Lewin taking the goals and the penalties. Bahoya now competes for his place.
verdicts.trigger: A return at Brighton. A £6.4m midfielder who is neither the scorer nor the taker is the wrong Leeds player.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: Scored at Elland Road at £6.0m and Brentford have never lost a league game he has scored in. The squad is unchanged for Sunderland.
verdicts.trigger: Thiago rediscovering the shirt, or two blanks in a side that has drawn twice.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: 18 points at £5.7m, which is the best value in the midfield, and Brentford have kept five clean sheets at the Gtech this year.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks. A midfielder scoring at this price is the cheapest way to fill an eleven.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Owned by Sir Fergie, 11 points at £4.5m, and Brentford have kept five league clean sheets at home in 2026. Sunderland visit with two debutants.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the shirt to a new centre-back, or two goals conceded at the Gtech.

verdicts.name: Ajayi
verdicts.why: Predicted to start in the back three against a Villa side that is the only team in the league without a shot on target. Mr CR7 bought him on Friday.
verdicts.trigger: Norton-Cuffy starting ahead of him. The six arrivals are still a squad competing for places.

verdicts.name: Egan
verdicts.why: 17 points at £4.0m, two clean sheets, and predicted to keep his place in the back three against Villa. Two of the five bought him this week.
verdicts.trigger: Hull conceding twice at home to Villa, or one of the six deadline-day signings taking a centre-back shirt.

verdicts.name: Tzolakis
verdicts.why: 20 points from two clean sheets at £4.6m, and 18 summer signings have not touched the goalkeeper. Villa have had no shot on target this season.
verdicts.trigger: Hull conceding in both of the next two. Villa at home is the first honest test of the shape.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sports Mole's predicted Sunderland XI has Meunier and Reinildo at full-back and no Hume, with Danso and Fofana in line for debuts. Two of the five own him and one starts him.
verdicts.trigger: Left out at Brentford and this is a sack. He starts and keeps his place through Danso's arrival and it goes back to solid.

verdicts.name: Ballard
verdicts.why: Sir Fergie's third defender, 8 points at £5.0m, and predicted to keep his place at centre-back beside Mukiele with Danso arriving.
verdicts.trigger: Danso taking his shirt. Two starts beside the new man and this is settled.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Predicted to start at Brentford, but Sunderland won without him producing anything and Fofana has arrived to take shots.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Villa have lost both and are the only team without a shot on target this season. Predicted to start at Hull, which does not change the price.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three with him playing all of them. Nothing shorter.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Owned by two of the five at a club that is bottom, has not scored in two, and has left its top scorer out of the squad. Forest have won their last four against Spurs.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 once players are settled and fixtures are softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Richarlison
verdicts.why: Spurs left him out of their Premier League squad entirely, and De Zerbi says he decided everything himself. He cannot be selected before January.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. A player outside the registered squad is an empty slot.

verdicts.name: Gibbs-White
verdicts.why: 17 league goal involvements in 2026, second only to B.Fernandes, on penalties, with Spurs at home. Nobody in the room owns him at £7.9m.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks, or Forest's midfield changing shape around him under Glasner.

verdicts.name: Thomas
verdicts.why: 11 points at £4.0m, but Coventry have not scored this season and Lampard's side has not kept a clean sheet in 18 matches. On Sir Fergie's bench for the Etihad.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet at home to Brighton in GW4, the kindest fixture on the ticker. Without it £4.0m is a bench slot.

signals.text: Mosquera's flag arrived on Saturday morning at 75%, two days after he missed Thursday's open training. Bruno Guimarães is flagged with a knock. Timber is back in full training but bench at best. Rice trained and is expected to start.
signals.action: Konsa is the Arsenal defender to expect on Sunday in place of Mosquera. White and Calafiori keep their places. Nobody in the room needs to move a defender before this one.

signals.text: Caicedo lasted under 20 minutes as a substitute against Brighton and is a major doubt for the Emirates. Henderson and Palestra are out until around the Hull game. Gusto and Lavia are expected in midfield, with James possibly in for Neto.
signals.action: Chelsea go to Arsenal with two stand-ins in central midfield and 18 games without a clean sheet. Their defenders and Martinez are not clean-sheet buys this week. Palmer, Rogers and João Pedro are unaffected.

signals.text: Sports Mole's predicted XI for Coventry has Guéhi back at centre-back beside Dias, Gvardiol at left-back, Nunes fit to compete with Khusanov at right-back, and Anderson and Bouaddi in the pivot. Enzo Fernández is ready for a full debut. Doku remains out. Ndiaye is available but Semenyo and Foden are expected wide.
signals.action: Gvardiol and Guéhi both in the back four is the version that keeps a clean sheet against a side that has not scored. O'Reilly is out of that eleven. Ndiaye is behind two wingers, so sell him if you own him.

signals.text: Jaissle says £51m Fernandez-Pardo will be eased in as a substitute, so Elanga, Wissa and Barnes continue. Burn, Livramento, Joelinton and Osula are all out. No team has faced more shots this season than Newcastle, 44 in two games.
signals.action: Elanga and Wissa keep their shirts against Bournemouth. Newcastle's attackers are the buy in front of the kindest run after Coventry. Their defenders are not, until the shot count comes down.

signals.text: Hinshelwood, Minteh, Mitoma, Wieffer, Tzimas and Ferguson are all out, with Rutter and Ayari only possible. Costinha may make his first start at right-back for Wieffer, and the predicted XI has De Cuyper in the attacking three again with Kadioglu at left-back.
signals.action: Two makeshift sides meet. Verbruggen's three owners start him anyway, because Leeds are improvising at centre-back too. De Cuyper is a winger this week, so do not expect defender returns from him.

signals.text: Farke: Rodon has a hamstring injury and "will be out for, at the moment, an assessment of eight to 10 weeks". Elvedi may get his first league start beside Bijol and Muharemovic, Gruev is back in training, Gudmundsson is a doubt, and Bard and Bahoya could debut. Nmecha came on to play alongside Calvert-Lewin last week.
signals.action: Do not buy a Leeds defender before the international break. Calvert-Lewin stays the Leeds player to own, and he is on a bench in this room with Brighton missing six.

signals.text: Butland, Zambrano, Matazo, Gyabi and Hughes are out and Crooks will be assessed. The predicted XI keeps the back three of Ajayi, Egan and Mendy, with Norton-Cuffy and Coyle competing at wing-back and Iroegbunam and Mouzakitis contenders in midfield. Villa are the only Premier League side without a shot on target this season.
signals.action: The back three that kept two clean sheets is expected to start against a side yet to hit the target. The £4.0m Hull defenders are buys, and three of the five now own one.

signals.text: Danso and Fofana are both in line for debuts at Brentford. Diarra is out for six to eight weeks with a thigh injury. Sports Mole's predicted XI has Meunier, Mukiele, Ballard and Reinildo across the back and no Hume.
signals.action: Check the Sunderland team sheet before 3pm if you start Hume, and two of the five own him. Ballard is expected to keep his place. Le Fée is expected to start.

signals.text: Substituted on 73 minutes against Ipswich with muscle tightness and faces a late fitness test on a hamstring before Everton. Sports Mole reports no major concern and expects him to start in an unchanged back four.
signals.action: Check the team sheet at Everton. Dorgu is the cover if he misses it.

signals.text: Grealish is back at Everton on loan from City and Sports Mole says an immediate return to the first XI is not out of the question. The predicted XI has both of them behind Barry with Johnson on the right.
signals.action: Hold if you own him. The creative share is now split, so watch who takes the set pieces on Sunday.

signals.text: Flagged at 75% on Saturday morning after missing Thursday's open training. Sports Mole says he has not been ruled out but expects Konsa to make his full debut in his place.
signals.action: Nobody in the room owns him now. Konsa is the one to watch on Sunday.

signals.text: Came on against Brighton and was withdrawn again inside 20 minutes. Alonso called it precautionary. Sports Mole lists him as a major doubt with a possible return against Arsenal.
signals.action: Not a buy this week. The Hull game on 12 September is the first realistic start.

signals.text: Came on for Muñoz on 64 minutes at Ipswich for a 26-minute debut. Iraola: "He hadn't played a single minute since the World Cup so we had to be careful."
signals.action: Wait for a start. Gakpo moved to centre-forward when he came on, so the two can play together.

signals.text: Played central midfield at Ipswich while Araujo made his debut at right-back. The BBC rated him seven and wrote that Iraola should never use him at right-back.
signals.action: The right-back worry has a name now, and it is Araujo. Hold at £7.0m.

signals.text: Two goals inside nine minutes at Ipswich and a third ruled out for offside, then substituted on 64 with the game won. Iraola: "If Alex is fit and is available, he will produce the numbers."
signals.action: Early substitutions in won games are the price of owning him. Fulham at home is next.

signals.text: Nmecha came on to play alongside him against Brentford and assisted his equaliser. Leeds note he has played back-to-back full 90s and scored against Brighton, Newcastle and Palace last season, his next three opponents.
signals.action: Start him. One of his five owners in the room has him on the bench at Brighton.

doctrine.text: Protecting your rank has a real cost. Price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template players are the default owns. Passing on them needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice. Sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul only tells you about one match. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week. Then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used. It is also the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up. Ignore the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position. Two of the room's bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro. None owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

An open window changes who plays before it changes who you should buy. Buy after the window shuts. It paid on 1 September. Two of the five went to bed owning an Everton midfielder and woke up owning a Manchester City substitute, and nobody who waited lost anything by waiting.

A cup tie tells you about the team sheet more than the result. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything. That is why a 35-year-old's header, a flagged striker's replacement and a vice-captain's absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need 90 minutes. Deadline day settled six calls here without a ball being kicked. They were the Liverpool winger, the Arsenal forward, the United left-back, the Everton striker, the Everton midfielder and the City left-back. A trigger only a scoreline can fire sits open through the weeks that decide the player.

A room that agrees has no protection against being wrong together. Not one of the five captained Haaland this week. The three who did in GW1 all moved off him. He scored twice at Palace before any of their captains had kicked a ball. Check what the room has agreed on, not only what it argues about.

Grade a rule by what it cost. Do not grade it by how sensible it sounded. D5 declined the £4.0m Hull defenders after one haul because they were flagged and it was one match. Two weeks on Hull have six points, two clean sheets, and the two best-scoring £4.0m defenders in the game. A rule that only ever says no stops being useful.

A Bench Boost wants 15 players who start. It does not need a double gameweek. The page called Sir Fergie's chip premature on Saturday. By Sunday night every one of his 15 had played, and it had won him the week and the lead. Grade a chip by the team sheet it lands on. The calendar does not matter.

A player sold inside the league has not gone, he has just moved clubs. The price on his card does not move for a week either. Ndiaye is worth £6.0m in two of these squads this morning and is fourth in the queue at his new club. Read the new shirt, forget the old fee.

Do not grade a player on 45 minutes. Three sacks were reversed on Wednesday. They were a winger hooked at half-time, a defender who came on as a substitute, and a left-back who was never actually dropped. It happened again on Thursday. The Hull back four sacked on Monday for six deadline-day arrivals turns out to be the back four the head coach intends to keep. Wait for the second data point when the first one is a substitution.

The injury flag moves last, after the news is already out. Arsenal's centre-back missed Thursday's open training with Chelsea to come and carries no flag in the player file. The £75m midfielder beside him missed it too. A squad that is picked on Friday afternoon is reported on Thursday night and flagged on Saturday morning. Read the training ground first, then the file.

roast.text: Sir Fergie played his Bench Boost in a plain single gameweek, all 15 of his players started, and it won him the week and a 29-point lead. He spent the one chip that rewards having no idea who to bench on the one week he had no idea who to bench.

plan.outlook: Saturday, one fixture into GW3. Friday night at Ipswich settled three of Thursday's triggers the right way. Kerkez kept a clean sheet, Gakpo made both goals with Barcola on the bench, and Szoboszlai played in midfield while Araujo debuted at right-back. All five captained Haaland at home to a Coventry side that has not scored. The Special One played his Wildcard from last place with 12 changes and had 16 points from Friday night alone. Sunday decides the rest: Mosquera is flagged and Konsa is expected to start at the Emirates, Chelsea arrive with two stand-ins in midfield, and Shaw has a hamstring test at Everton. The GW4 deadline is a week away, so nobody needs a transfer before the derby is read.

rows.name: Wildcard
rows.window: The Special One played his in GW3. For the other four, GW6 to GW8 is the first honest window, once three settled line-ups exist

rows.name: Free Hit
rows.window: hold for a blank gameweek; none scheduled yet

rows.name: Bench Boost
rows.window: wants 15 players who start, which is a settled squad rather than a double

rows.name: Triple Captain
rows.window: a premium on a home double, or not at all

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). Three of the five have now spent one. Le Professeur's Bench Boost returned six points in GW1, Sir Fergie's returned 151 and the lead, and The Special One played his Wildcard in GW3 from last place with 12 changes. Two of the five have played nothing. The window is shut and the squads stop moving under the chip now, so the four who hold a Wildcard should read three settled line-ups before GW6.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.

Saturday of a gameweek one fixture old. Upgraded Cherki to nailed on the start his trigger asked for, plus two goals at Selhurst Park, and recorded that not one of the five captained Haaland before he scored twice. Moved Guéhi back towards a buy once Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back. Settled Watkins on the £50m Al-Hilal sale and Martinez on Villa confirming the Chelsea deal. Opened Foden, O'Reilly, Diouf, Delap and Muñoz. Recommended no transfer again, on the grounds that the window shuts on Tuesday and the GW3 deadline is the Friday after it — the first week of the season in which waiting costs nothing. Minted D12 on the armband.

Saturday's five fixtures settled four open triggers and opened a hole. Upgraded Tarkowski to solid on the late goal at Bournemouth, exactly the trigger written on Thursday. Sacked Tonali, whose trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle and who was substituted in a 2-0 defeat, and sacked Gravenberch, who was left out of the pivot rather than keeping a clean sheet in it. Moved Igor Jesus back to watch after he started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, and cooled Delap for the same reason. Cooled Kerkez after he was taken off on 71 minutes, and cooled Woltemade after Wissa scored at Spurs and Napoli were reported to want him on loan. Settled Sánchez and Muñoz by transfer. Opened Isak, Gibbs-White, Elanga, Wissa, Scott and the three Hull picks. Minted D13 against the brain's own D5: the £4.0m Hull defenders it declined after one haul now have two clean sheets behind them and thirty-six points between them. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday.

Gameweek 2 settled everything except Villa v Arsenal. Marked the brain's own Bench Boost rule under review after Sir Fergie played one in a single gameweek and won the week and the lead with it — D14. Upgraded B.Fernandes on a hat-trick that fired his blank trigger the other way, and upgraded Maguire, Lammens, Schade, Calvert-Lewin, Wissa, Ajayi and Tzolakis. Sacked Lacroix on the exact trigger written on Thursday — a clean sheet against a depleted Brighton — after Chelsea conceded three and reached eighteen games without one. Sacked Caicedo, who came off in tears after eleven minutes, Kerkez a week early on the substitution rather than the missed start, Welbeck on an unused bench at 4-3, and Woltemade once Wissa started and scored. Cooled Ndiaye with Spurs in advanced talks, Semenyo on one assist at £8.5m, De Cuyper on an advanced role that is not the position he was bought for, and Havertz on Arsenal chasing Álvarez. Opened Rashford, Neto and Groß. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday, with the deadline three days behind it.

First run with the window shut. Recommended the room's first transfers of the season. Ndiaye out for Mr CR7 and Le Professeur after his £65m move to Manchester City, and Aït-Nouri out for The Special One on City calling him third-choice left-back. Reversed three sacks that deadline day settled the other way. Gakpo stays after Liverpool rejected £80m. Shaw keeps his place after United failed to sign a left-back. Barry becomes Everton's only striker after the Balogun deal collapsed. Sacked Tzolis on a 4/10 and a half-time substitution, and Konsa on coming off the bench rather than starting. Cooled Cherki, Foden and Semenyo on City signing two more attackers, and cooled the whole Hull back four on six deadline-day arrivals and the sale of a defender who had played all three games. Promoted D9 to doctrine on the evidence it just produced, retired D6 into D14, and minted D15 on players sold inside the league.

Deadline eve. Reversed three of Monday's own sacks after reading the window post-mortems. Tzolis was graded on 45 minutes, but impressed in the Community Shield and on the opening day. Konsa was signed because Saliba and Timber are injured, and the man ahead of him limped off. Kerkez stays because Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola knows him from Bournemouth. Upgraded Gvardiol to nailed on City saying O'Reilly moves into midfield, which reverses last week's trigger. Downgraded Szoboszlai on Liverpool naming him as right-back cover, and Gakpo on Barcola's likely debut at Ipswich. Upgraded Ajayi on the flag coming off. Recommended captaincy calls rather than transfers for three of the five, and minted D16. A verdict written on 45 minutes proves nothing.

Deadline day, window shut. Read the training ground rather than the player file. Mosquera and Bruno Guimarães both missed Arsenal's open session on Thursday. Downgraded Mosquera without a flag, moved Konsa and White up, and told Le Professeur to promote Konsa off his bench rather than spend a transfer. Reversed Monday's cooling of the Hull back four after Jakirovic said the six deadline-day arrivals must earn shirts, and put Ajayi back on the house list. Opened Barcola, Guéhi and Bruno G., and sacked Richarlison outright. He was left out of Spurs' registered Premier League squad. Upgraded Verbruggen on Rodon's eight-to-ten-week hamstring and Leeds improvising at centre-back. Repeated the Ndiaye transfer for the two owners and the Aït-Nouri sale for The Special One. Minted D17. The flag moves last.

Saturday, one fixture into GW3. Friday night at Ipswich settled three of Thursday's triggers the right way. Kerkez kept the clean sheet his trigger asked for, Gakpo made both goals with Barcola on the bench, and Szoboszlai played in midfield while Araujo debuted at right-back. Upgraded all three to solid and opened Isak, Jacquet and Araujo. Read the deadline. All five captained Haaland and The Special One played his Wildcard from last place with 12 changes. Mr CR7 sold Ndiaye and started Calvert-Lewin as recommended. Le Professeur sold Konsa the day before every predicted Arsenal XI named him. Downgraded Shaw on a hamstring fitness test, Hume on a predicted Sunderland XI without him, and Dewsbury-Hall on Grealish's return. Downgraded Mosquera again as the flag arrived on Saturday morning, two days after the training report, which is D17 holding once. Rewrote the Team radar for the Saturday and Sunday team sheets. No transfer recommended. The GW4 deadline is a week away and Sunday's derby decides four Arsenal and Chelsea calls.
